MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.




About the Role



Oracle Fusion Application Analyst




Key support role - Oracle Fusion Cloud (ERP-SCM) environment


Provide functional and technical support for Monash Health's critical enterprise application.


Permanent, full time role, based at Scoresby Corporate Site




Monash Health is the largest healthcare provider in Victoria and is recognised for its exceptional clinical care and research. We are dedicated to providing outstanding patient care. We appreciate our unique and vital role as an integral part of the communities we serve and the importance of maintaining our services in a changing environment. The integrity of our corporate systems is critical to our ability to deliver excellent care to every patient, every time.



This role represents a great opportunity within our newly formed Applications and Enablement team. Reporting to the Manager Finance Systems, you'll be part of a team responsible for ensuring our systems perform reliably and consistently, delivering both business continuity and continuous improvement. Working closely with business stakeholders, vendors and in-house digital teams, you'll play an integral role in optimising Oracle Fusion to help Monash Health deliver tomorrow's care today.



If appointed, your contribution will be assessed across five Key Result Areas:




Operational Support


System Configuration and Maintenance


Stakeholder Engagement


Continuous Improvement


Governance, Risk and Compliance




This role is expected to work in a hybrid model, with a minimum of three days per week on site in our Scoresby Office.




About you


The Oracle Application Analyst ensures the effective integration of technology with all business functions to maximize organisational performance. Develops and maintains positive relationships between Business Services and its customers. With strong system knowledge and highly developed communication skills you can demonstrate the ability to translate technical problems into language that's easy to understand for non-technical stakeholders. 



Naturally curious, you readily analyse business processes and translate requirements into system solutions. Above all, you are a committed team player who enjoys working collaboratively with colleagues to provide a consistently high level of service to your stakeholders. 



On a personal level, you are:




Highly organised


Flexible and able to adapt readily to changing priorities 


A highly effective communicator, with active listening skills


Sound technical understanding of systems and related business processes




What you need



To be considered for this role, you will need to demonstrate:




Tertiary qualification in Information Technology or Business 


Strong functional knowledge of one or more Oracle Fusion modules (ERP, EPM, SCM)


Experience working within an Application Managed Services (AMS) or shared services support model


Proven ability to analyse incidents, identify root causes and coordinate resolution across a number of teams


Demonstrated experience providing Level 2 and Level 3 application support for Oracle Fusion Could, in a complex enterprise environment


Experience with incident, problem and change management in an enterprise environment




While not mandatory requirements, experience with the following will be highly regarded:




Supporting integrations, reporting and security roles within Oracle Fusion


Oracle Fusion reporting tools (OTBI and BI Publisher) 


Familiarity with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) and enterprise integrations




We are especially interested in hearing from you if you've worked in a large public sector or healthcare organisation. 




Benefits of working at Monash Health




Monash Health offers a range of benefits, including: 




Comprehensive employee health and wellbeing programs including Fitness Passport


Five weeks annual leave with leave loading


Monthly ADOs for full-time employees 


Salary packaging benefits



For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out to Sherree O'Connell, Head of Enterprise Corporate Applications and Enablement on 0451 309 776


Position Description can be found here





Our Culture and Values 






At Monash Health, our people are at the heart of everything we do. Our culture is inclusive, supportive and future-focused, underpinned by clear values and a commitment to continuous improvement. 







Our teams play a critical role in bringing our new strategy to life, challenging traditional approaches, embracing innovation, and ensuring every appointment reflects our commitment to equity, transparency and excellence. 







You'll be encouraged to share ideas, contribute to improvement initiatives, and grow alongside experienced professionals who are passionate about what they do. 







We are Full Hearted, Open Minded and All In, enabling excellent service delivery and a positive candidate and employee experience every time. 







We recognise the value of equal employment opportunity. We are committed to patient safety, promoting fairness, equity and diversity in the workplace and to Child Safe Standards. 





How to Apply


Applications are accepted via the Monash Health online EHub system. For information including how to apply and probity check requirements, please click here for the 'Application Guide'


Applications will be screened upon receipt and selection activity may commence prior to the closing date.

## Cyber Security Operations Coordinator
## Position Overview
We are looking for a skilled and proactive Cyber Security Operations Coordinator to lead the coordination and response to complex cyber security incidents, threat hunting investigations, and cross-functional security operations. This role plays a critical part in safeguarding organisational systems and data by driving incident response activities, advising leadership on operational matters, and contributing to strategic security planning. The ideal candidate is a technically proficient security professional with strong coordination capabilities, sound analytical judgement, and the ability to communicate complex security issues clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
## Key Responsibilities
- Lead the end-to-end investigation and response to cyber security incidents, including containment, mitigation, and recovery activities, ensuring timely resolution and minimal operational disruption
- Direct threat hunting operations to proactively identify threat vectors, develop threat models, and build security cases that inform defensive strategies across the organisation
- Analyse security risks, vulnerabilities, and emerging threats, translating findings into actionable security plans and technical controls aligned with the organisation's security architecture
- Coordinate and manage tasks across multiple teams during incident response and threat hunt engagements, ensuring clear communication, accountability, and effective workflow throughout each operation
- Advise senior leadership on the status of current security operations, ongoing collaborations, and key findings, contributing meaningfully to strategic security planning and policy development
- Develop and communicate key messaging around security incidents and threat intelligence, ensuring accurate and timely information is delivered to the appropriate stakeholders
- Oversee the collection, preservation, and forensic analysis of digital evidence in accordance with established procedures and chain-of-custody requirements
- Implement and maintain technical security controls that align with the organisation's security strategies, frameworks, and compliance obligations
- Perform ongoing threat management activities, monitoring threat landscapes and updating security models to reflect evolving attack techniques and adversary behaviours
- Facilitate and coordinate security awareness training programmes for staff, promoting a security-conscious culture across the organisation
- Maintain detailed records of incident response activities, investigation findings, and operational outcomes to support continuous improvement and audit readiness
- Collaborate with internal teams and external partners to uphold the integrity, confidentiality, and availability of organisational systems and information assets
## Required Qualifications & Skills
- Bachelor's degree in Cyber Security, Information Technology, Computer Science, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience
- Demonstrated experience in a cyber security operations, incident response, or threat intelligence role, with exposure to coordinating cross-functional teams
- Strong working knowledge of incident response methodologies, threat hunting techniques, and digital forensics processes
- Experience conducting security risk assessments, vulnerability analyses, and developing actionable remediation plans
- Proficiency with security tools and platforms such as SIEM, EDR, IDS/IPS, and threat intelligence feeds
- Solid understanding of security frameworks and standards, including NIST, ISO 27001, or the Australian Cyber Security Centre (ACSC) Essential Eight
- Demonstrated ability to analyse and interpret complex technical information and communicate findings clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences
- Strong project coordination and task management skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities in a high-pressure environment
- Sound understanding of network security, endpoint protection, identity and access management, and cloud security principles
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with experience producing professional reports, briefings, and incident documentation
## Preferred Qualifications
- Industry certifications such as CISSP, CISM, CEH, GIAC (e.g. GCIH, GCFA), or CompTIA Security+
- Experience working within a Security Operations Centre (SOC) environment or managed security services setting
- Familiarity with Australian regulatory and compliance requirements, including the Privacy Act, Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, and relevant sector-specific obligations
- Exposure to threat intelligence platforms, malware analysis, or reverse engineering
- Experience contributing to the development of security policies, procedures, or organisational security awareness programmes
- Prior experience briefing or advising senior leadership or executive stakeholders on cyber security matters
## Why Join Us?
- Be part of a collaborative and forward-thinking security team where your contributions directly shape the organisation's cyber resilience
- Access ongoing professional development opportunities, including support for industry certifications, training programmes, and conference attendance
- Enjoy a flexible working environment that supports work-life balance, including hybrid work arrangements
- Competitive remuneration package with superannuation, reflective of your skills and experience
- Work within a values-driven organisation committed to innovation, integrity, and building a diverse and inclusive workplace
## Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Superannuation

St Vincent's Private Hospital Toowoomba is seeking an accomplished Business Development Manager to lead specialist engagement, doctor recruitment and strategic growth initiatives across one of Queensland's most respected private hospitals.

We are looking for an experienced and strategic Cyber Security Architect to lead the design and implementation of advanced security systems across enterprise environments. This role is responsible for developing security architecture frameworks, identifying cyber risks, and delivering secure-by-design solutions that align with business goals and compliance standards.
The ideal candidate will have deep expertise in security controls, cloud security, enterprise infrastructure, and governance frameworks, and will play a lead role in defining the organisation’s cyber defence strategy.
Key Responsibilities:
Design, develop, and maintain enterprise-wide security architecture covering infrastructure, applications, data, identity, and cloud platforms.
Lead security assessments, threat modelling, and risk analysis during the solution design phase for new systems or services.
Define and implement security reference architectures and ensure adherence to frameworks such as NIST, ISO 27001, CIS Controls, and Zero Trust.
Oversee the integration of security tools and controls across network, endpoint, identity, and cloud layers (e.g., SIEM, EDR, CASB, IAM, firewalls).
Collaborate with software engineers, DevOps teams, and cloud architects to embed security-by-design principles in SDLC and CI/CD pipelines.
Review security incidents and recommend architectural enhancements to improve resilience and reduce attack surfaces.
Develop and maintain policies, procedures, and architectural documentation, ensuring alignment with internal governance and external regulatory requirements.
Act as a key stakeholder in incident response planning, disaster recovery architecture, and business continuity strategies.
Provide technical guidance and leadership to security engineering and operations teams, and advise executives on cyber risks.
Liaise with vendors, regulators, and third parties to ensure security architecture is compliant and up to date with emerging threats.
Required Qualifications & Skills:
Bachelor’s degree (or higher) in Cyber Security, Computer Science, Information Technology, or related discipline.
5+ years of experience in cyber security with at least 2–3 years in security architecture or design roles.
Strong understanding of network security, encryption, identity management, cloud security (AWS/Azure/GCP), and endpoint protection.
Proficiency with security technologies such as SIEM, IDS/IPS, IAM, MFA, EDR, firewalls, VPNs, and vulnerability scanners.
Hands-on experience designing secure systems in cloud-native, hybrid, or on-premise environments.
Strong knowledge of cybersecurity standards and frameworks (e.g., NIST, ISO 27001, ASD Essential Eight, OWASP).
Excellent documentation, stakeholder engagement, and risk communication skills.
Desirable:
Relevant certifications such as SABSA, CISSP, CISM, AWS Security, Azure Security Engineer, TOGAF.
Experience in Zero Trust Architecture, DevSecOps, or secure multi-cloud environments.
Background in regulated industries such as finance, healthcare, critical infrastructure, or government.
Familiarity with threat intelligence platforms, security automation, and SOAR tools.

Permanent Residents (PR) and Australian Citizens are eligible to apply
Job Type: Full-time
Salary: $70,000 to $120,000 per year + Super

We are a leading supplier of concrete lifting systems, specialised fastening solutions, and construction products to the precast, tilt-up, and general concreting sectors. We work closely with builders, contractors, and construction professionals, providing reliable products and practical solutions for projects of all sizes.  With more than 40 years of industry experience, we have built a reputation for product knowledge, technical expertise, and exceptional customer service. Our team understands the demands of the construction industry and is committed to helping customers source the right products quickly and efficiently.  By combining quality products with expert advice and dependable service, we continue to be a trusted partner for construction professionals throughout Australia.
We are now seeking a Management Consultant to join our team.  This role involves being responsible for analysing and improving our operational, commercial, marketing and business management practices to enhance organisational performance, profitability, customer satisfaction and strategic growth. You will need to provide expert business advice to management, identifying operational improvements, evaluating market opportunities and support the implementation of systems, processes and strategic initiatives across the organisation. We are offering $110K - $120K
Key Duties:
•	Analyse and evaluate operational procedures, business systems and organisational structures to identify opportunities for improved efficiency, productivity and profitability.
•	Gather, interpret and evaluate operational, financial and commercial data to support informed business decision-making. 
•	Conduct reviews of policies, procedures and workflows and recommend practical improvements to business processes and performance. 
•	Develop business cases, feasibility assessments and strategic recommendations to support organisational growth and continuous improvement. 
•	Monitor budgets, financial performance and key business metrics, providing analysis and recommendations to improve profitability. 
•	Design, implement and maintain KPI reporting frameworks to measure operational effectiveness and business outcomes 
•	Conduct market research, competitor analysis and SWOT assessments to identify new business opportunities and industry trends. 
•	Evaluate and recommend new technologies, systems and business solutions to enhance organisational capability and efficiency. 
•	Lead and support business improvement projects, including process redesign, change management and implementation activities. 
•	Prepare and present reports, findings and recommendations to management, supporting strategic and operational decision-making. 
•	Provide ongoing management consulting services to support business growth, operational excellence and achievement of company objectives
Qualifications and Experience
•	Bachelor’s degree or higher qualification in Marketing, Business, or a related field
•	At least 3 years of full-time relevant marketing experience in business analysis, management consulting, operational improvement or related positions.
•	Demonstrated experience in business analysis, strategic planning, budgeting, market research, process improvement, stakeholder engagement, and systems implementation

MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Monash Health exists to reimagine care, so that people can live their best lives. 






We provide safe and equitable care, for every stage of life, delivered with world-leading expertise and over 175 years of experience. 






As a leading academic health service, we're committed to providing tomorrow's care today by integrating research, teaching and training into everyday practice. 






Our team of 24,000 people are full hearted, open minded and all in. Together, we provide more than 250 integrated services for every stage of life at over 50 locations and in the community across south-east Melbourne, Victoria, serving 1.2 million residents in the South Metro Local Health Service Network. 


Are you currently part of the team at Monash Health? Use your network login to access the Monash Health Careers portal and discover all the job opportunities open to you, to support growing your career within the organisation.




To see first-hand what our colleagues think about working here, take a look at the following short videos monashhealth.org-careers.








Data Analyst- Statistician- Research Assistant - MCHRI (Monash Centre for Health Research & Implementation), Monash Medical Centre Clayton 






Employment Type: Fixed term Full-time for 12 months with a view to extending 






Start & End Date: July-Aug 2026 - July-Aug 2027 






Hours p.w: 30.8-38 hours p.w (0.8 EFT-1.0EFT) 







We have x2 Data Analyst- Statistician- Research Assistant positions available.






The Data Analyst-Statistician will provide statistical and analytic support for Monash Health HREC ethics applications, statistical consultations for Monash Health staff and students, and project coordination and management for data and analytics components of research projects at MCHRI. In consultation with Professor Helena Teede and A-Prof Joanne Enticott, the Data Analyst-Statistician will undertake research and analytic work needed to support the Monash Centre for Health Research & Implementation and the biostatistical consulting service for Monash Health staff and students. 







About Monash Centre for Health Research and Implementation (MCHRI), Monash University and Monash Health 






MCHRI sits under the Faculty of Medicine, Nursing and Health Sciences at Monash University. Established in 2005, MCHRI has grown from 3 to 180 staff and students. MCHRI is a collaborative partnership between Monash University and Monash Health, a women's health and implementation Centre. MCHRI utilises public health research as well as the translation and implementation of clinical, health services and public health knowledge, underpinned by cross-sector end-user engagement, to deliver health impact. MCHRI is the base for the maternity Learning Health System (LHS), embedding research and maternal healthcare provision to drive sustainable improvement in maternity care and health outcomes for women and newborns. 






Read more about MCHRI research at: https:--mchri.org.au-about-mchri-vision-and-overview- 












About the Role 






Located at Monash Health within the Monash Health Translation Precinct, MCHRI is expanding its biostatistical consultancy and research analytics capability. The Data Analyst-Statistician will provide research statistical support to the Monash Health HREC, provide statistical consultations for Monash Health staff and students, and support data-analytics components of research projects. The existing highly skilled biostatistical consultancy team provides a supportive environment and structured mentorship for new members to upskill. Primary responsibilities include: 







Provide research statistical support to the Monash Health HREC, including statistical review and reporting for ethics applications.


Provide statistical consultations for Monash Health staff and students. 


Coordinate and manage data and analytics components of MCHRI research projects. 


Assist with evaluation methodologies, data cleaning, data analysis, interpretation and preparation of results and reports. 


Assist in preparing documentation including ethics and governance submissions, grant applications, research reports, conference abstracts and manuscripts. 


Maintain and use information systems, databases, websites and record-keeping systems that support MCHRI research projects and programs. 


Keep abreast of developments in biostatistics, data science, risk prediction and health research methods through literature, meetings and seminars. 


Comply with Monash Health and Monash University policies, procedures and protocols relevant to undertaking research. 








About You 






We are seeking a highly motivated quantitative researcher with strong statistical, analytic and problem-solving skills. You will be able to communicate statistical methods and results clearly to multidisciplinary research and clinical teams, manage competing priorities and work effectively under pressure. Experience in health, healthcare, women's health, maternity, emergency health data, clinical datasets, risk prediction or implementation-ready analytics would be advantageous. 






Machine learning skills are desirable but not compulsory. The role is suitable for a statistician, data analyst, epidemiologist, research assistant or data scientist with experience in health, clinical, public health or research settings. 







What you need: 







Tertiary qualification in statistics, biostatistics, epidemiology, data science, public health, biomedical science, health sciences, information technology or a related discipline. 


Salary is negotiable and commensurate with experience. 


Quantitative research experience, including data cleaning, data management, statistical analysis and reporting. 


Knowledge of statistical analysis software such as Stata, R and-or Python; experience with reproducible workflows and script-based analysis is desirable. 


Experience in statistical consultancy, teaching, health research or clinical research support would be advantageous. 


Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively with clinicians, researchers, statisticians, data scientists, project managers and data custodians. 


Excellent interpersonal, written and oral communication skills, including the ability to produce clear reports, tables, figures and documentation. 


Understanding of confidentiality, privacy, human research ethics, information security and responsible research data management. 


Experience with risk prediction, electronic medical record data, pathology data, biobank data, biomarker research, machine learning or women's health research is highly desirable. 











For a confidential discussion and to explore this opportunity further, please reach out toJoanne Enticott by email at joanne.enticott@monash.edu.
